nodes.label: desktop memory - the v1 tag pollution is a designed output of two facets

Frozen copy taken 2026-08-03 of the desktop machine's memory file - the live directory sits on the other machine and is not reachable from here, so this copy is what there is to review. Listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md section 6. The v1 tag pollution is a designed output of the facets, not random noise. The v1 tagger design: 5 facets, verified in the pipeline source - topic, entities, activity, temporal, evidence - each a per-chunk LLM lens; w_chunk = strength x coverage_bonus, where strength is the square root of the mean of squared facet strengths and coverage_bonus is concentration raised to COVERAGE_ALPHA at 0.25, with MULTI_FACET_THRESHOLD at 0.50; and a separate score stage producing relevance_to_file. The causal link: about 18% of 24,804 tags are junk, eid_* plus years and dates, with eid alone about 16k HAS_TAG edges - the temporal facet manufactures date tags, the entities facet reads eid_ strings in flattened prose and emits them as entity tags at about 15k LLM-emitted eid edges, and the evidence facet produces identifier-ish URL and PR tags. The root: the chunker flattened ids, dates and links into prose, the tagger was told to tag entities, time and evidence, and it obliged. The crucial correction from the user on 2026-05-30: facets are semantic dimensions, not extractors - temporal was never a date string but the time-relationship of the content, retrospective versus now versus forward-looking, spans, ongoing concern, urgency - so structure takes the literal FACT while the facet keeps its intended MEANING, and v1 conflated the two. CANON_AUDIT.md 6.5 and 6.9 flag this file as one of three declaring a different settled facet set, and as naming a fourth model for the tagger role
